what_its_for: Raltegravir is an antiviral medicine used to treat HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) infection in adults and children. It works by blocking an enzyme called integrase that HIV needs to multiply in your body. This helps lower the amount of HIV in your blood and keeps your immune system stronger. Raltegravir does not cure HIV, but it helps control the infection when used with other HIV medicines.
how_to_take: Take raltegravir exactly as your doctor prescribes. You can take the regular tablets (400 mg) with or without food. The chewable tablets can be chewed or swallowed whole and can also be taken with or without food. The oral granules (powder for babies and young children) should be mixed with a small amount of liquid before giving. Do NOT crush or split the 600 mg high-dose tablets (Isentress HD) — swallow them whole. Always take raltegravir together with your other HIV medicines as directed.
dosing: Your dose depends on your age, weight, and which form of raltegravir you are using. Common adult doses are: 400 mg tablet twice a day, OR 1200 mg (two 600 mg tablets) once a day. Children's doses are based on body weight. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own. Take your doses at the same time(s) every day to keep the medicine working well.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is not too close to the time for your next dose. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Missing doses can allow HIV to grow and become harder to treat, so try your best to take every dose on time.
storage: Store raltegravir tablets and chewable tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep them in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect the medicine from moisture. The oral granules (for children) should also be stored at room temperature and used within 30 minutes of mixing with liquid. Keep all forms of raltegravir out of reach of children and pets. Do not use medicine that has expired.
what_to_avoid: Do not skip doses or stop taking raltegravir without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel well. Avoid taking antacids that contain aluminum or magnesium (such as Maalox or Mylanta) at the same time as raltegravir, because they can lower how much medicine gets into your body. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, including rifampin (a tuberculosis drug), which can lower raltegravir levels. Raltegravir does not prevent passing HIV to others, so continue to practice safe sex and do not share needles.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: a serious skin rash, blistering, peeling, or sores in your mouth or eyes; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain; signs of muscle problems such as unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness; mental health changes such as depression, unusual thoughts, or thoughts of harming yourself; signs of an immune reaction (your immune system getting stronger and reacting to old infections, causing fever, swollen lymph nodes, or breathing problems); or any unusual or severe side effect.
when_it_works: Raltegravir starts working right away, but you may not feel different at first. After a few weeks, blood tests should show that your HIV viral load (the amount of HIV in your blood) is going down and your CD4 count (immune cells) is going up. It may take several months to reach an undetectable viral load. Keep taking your medicine every day, even when you feel healthy — stopping it allows HIV to come back and get stronger.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Raltegravir is commonly used during pregnancy and is considered a preferred HIV medicine for pregnant women. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Children: Raltegravir can be used in newborns, infants, and children; the dose and form used depend on the child's weight. Older adults: Older patients can use raltegravir, but should be monitored more closely for side effects. Liver or kidney problems: Raltegravir generally does not require dose changes for liver or kidney disease, but always tell your doctor about any health conditions you have.
